name: Crossing the Delaware
summary: At dusk the army begins to cross the Delaware at McKonkey's Ferry in Durham boats and ferries, in sleet and floating ice; the crossing runs about three hours late.

name: Alarm at Trenton
summary: A party fires on the Pennington road picket on Christmas evening; the garrison turns out and the post is reinforced.

name: Crossing complete
summary: The last troops and guns reach the New Jersey bank, about three hours late. Knox had the infantry over by about 02:00; the Army's campaign history has 03:00, with the guns an hour later.

name: March begins
summary: The column sets off for Trenton, about nine miles away.
playback_text: The column sets off from the landing for Trenton, about nine miles away.

name: Army divides
summary: At Birmingham Greene takes the upper road and Sullivan the River Road.

name: First shots
summary: Greene's advance drives in Lt. Wiederhold's picket on the Pennington Road.
playback_text: Greene's advance drives in Lt. Wiederhold's picket on the Pennington road.

name: Sullivan's attack
summary: About three minutes later the lower column strikes the jäger picket at the Hermitage.

name: Guns open
summary: Forrest's and Hamilton's batteries open from the head of King and Queen Streets.

name: Hessian guns taken
summary: The Rall regiment's two guns are lost on King Street, just north of the headquarters.

name: Line of battle
summary: The three regiments form a line along the east edge of the village.
playback_text: The three Hessian regiments form a line along the east edge of the village.

name: Rall shot
summary: Rall leads the Rall and Lossberg regiments back into the town and is mortally wounded on Queen Street.
playback_text: Rall leads two regiments back into the town and is mortally wounded on Queen Street.

name: Surrender in the orchard
summary: Lt. Col. Scheffer surrenders the Rall and von Lossberg regiments in the orchard east of the town.

name: Knyphausen surrenders
summary: The Knyphausen regiment, cut off from the bridge, surrenders by the Assunpink a quarter mile away, shortly after the others. About fifty men get over the creek.

name: Return to Pennsylvania
summary: The army starts back across the Delaware with its prisoners.

name: Escape over the bridge
summary: The jägers and the twenty British dragoons get away over the Assunpink bridge before Sullivan's men reach it.

name: The escapers get away
summary: The British dragoons reach Princeton, the jägers Bordentown, and about fifty men of the Knyphausen regiment, who forded the Assunpink, make for Crosswicks. Some 400 to 600 of the garrison got away in all.

name: Morgan forms for battle
summary: About an hour before daylight a scout reports Tarleton within five miles. Morgan turns his men out and puts them in three lines across the Green River Road: riflemen in front, Pickens's militia behind them, and Howard's Continentals and Virginians on the rise behind, with Washington's cavalry in reserve.

name: The pickets are driven in
summary: About day, Tarleton's advance guard of Legion dragoons drives in Capt. Inman's mounted pickets on the Green River Road and finds the Americans drawn up to fight.

name: Tarleton deploys
summary: The British come out of the woods and form one line in sight of the Americans: light infantry on the right, the Legion infantry in the centre, the 7th Fusiliers on the left, a 3-pounder in each gap and fifty dragoons on each flank. The 71st Highlanders and about 200 Legion cavalry stand in reserve 150 yards back.

name: First shots
summary: Tarleton sends Ogilvie's Legion dragoons to drive in the riflemen in front. The riflemen fire from behind the trees and the dragoons come back with empty saddles. Militia veterans gave John Savage of Brandon's regiment the first shot.

name: The British line advances
summary: About sunrise the two guns open and the whole line comes on with three cheers. Morgan answers along the militia line: "They gave us the British halloo, boys, give them the Indian halloo."

name: The skirmishers fall back
summary: McDowell's and Cunningham's riflemen, having picked off officers at long range, fall back on Pickens's line.

name: The militia volleys
summary: Pickens's militia hold their fire until the British are within killing distance, then fire by regiments: "pop, pop, pop, and then a whole volley". The British line halts to dress and comes on again.

name: The militia withdraw; dragoons ride them down
summary: As ordered, the militia file off round Howard's line, most of them round its left, to re-form in rear. The 17th Light Dragoons on Tarleton's right charge after them towards their horses; Washington's cavalry strikes the dragoons and drives them back.

name: Line against line
summary: The British infantry close on Howard's line and the two fire at close range, neither giving way. Tarleton orders up the 71st on his left to turn Howard's right, and the reserve cavalry to follow it; the cavalry does not come.

name: Howard's line falls back
summary: Howard orders his right company to face the Highlanders. The order goes wrong; the company faces about, and the rest of the line, taking it for a retreat, marches to the rear in good order. Morgan picks the ground for it to halt, about 80 to 100 yards back.

name: Face about: volley and bayonet
summary: The British, sure the day is won, rush on out of order. At 10 to 30 yards Howard's line faces about and fires; then it charges with the bayonet. The British line stops, breaks and runs.

name: Double envelopment
summary: Washington's cavalry rides round the British right and into their rear; Pickens's militia come back into the fight round the American right, onto the 71st. The infantry throw down their arms. The gunners fight to the last by their two 3-pounders, which are taken.

name: Tarleton's last charge
summary: The Legion cavalry will not charge and about 200 of them leave the field. Tarleton leads some fifty horsemen, most of them of the 17th Light Dragoons, at the American cavalry and is beaten off; he and Washington cross swords before he rides away down the Green River Road.

name: Pursuit
summary: Washington and Pickens follow Tarleton for 22 to 24 miles without catching him; the British burn most of their baggage. Morgan counts over 500 prisoners, two guns and two colours for 12 killed and about 60 wounded, and marches off the field the same day to get the prisoners away from Cornwallis.
